input: nums is a plain list of integers in nondecreasing order; target is an integer. Preconditions are not checked at runtime.
return: A fresh two-integer list containing the first and last target indices, inclusive; [-1, -1] for an empty list or absent target. Duplicates are included in the returned range.
mutation_aliasing: No input writes, sorting or copies. The result never aliases nums. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: The paired contract restricts values and target to integers in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. Python integer comparisons and index arithmetic are exact. No target arithmetic is used.
complexity: O(log(n + 1)) time and O(1) auxiliary space, including the constant-sized fresh result, under constant-cost indexing and machine-word comparisons.

helpers.name: lower_bound
helpers.contract: Returns the first index whose value is at least target, or n; searches [left, right).
helpers.cost: One call, O(log(n + 1)) time and O(1) space. Its complete identical definition is included in each of the three search candidates.

helpers.name: upper_bound
helpers.contract: Returns the first index whose value is greater than target, or n; searches [left, right).
helpers.cost: At most one call, O(log(n + 1)) time and O(1) space; the complete definition is included here.
